IS: 8049-1 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR PLATFORM TRUCKS 
( Second Revision ) 



(Reaffirmed 2001) 



1. Scope— Covers the principal dimensions and requirements of platform trucks used for transpor- 
tation of goods. « 

2. Terminology— For the purpose of this standard, the following definition shall apply. 

2.1 Platform Truck — A platform truck is a load supporting truck consisting of platform made out of 
steel or wood, with wheels or castors which can be moved manually. 

3. Types 

3.1 Tilt Type — These trucks have the wheels or castors placed or mounted so that there shall be a 
tilting or balancing action around main or centre wheels (located at the longitudinal centreline) 
before either of the end wheels or castors come into contact with the floor. Such end wheels shall 
be of sliding type on axles. Castors, where used, shall be of swivel type and there shall be one 
castor at each end. 

3.2 Non-Tilt Type — These trucks have two swivel castors at the push handle end and two fixed 
castors at the other end, or two wheels mounted on axle at one end and two wheels made steerable 
by the turntable arrangement at the pull type handle end. All the wheels or castors shall be so 
mounted that the load will normally be distributed between all four wheels. 

4. Material — Deck shall be made of all wood or structural steel conforming to IS: 226-1975 
'Structural steel ( standard quality ) ( fifth revision)'. Frame shall be made of structural steel. Other 
tubular parts shall be made of mild steel tubes conforming to IS : 1239 ( Part 1 )-1979 'Specification 
for mild steel tubes (fourth revision)'. Decking, if made of wood, shall be of country teak wood, 
20 mm nominal finished thickness. 



5. Construction and Shape — The construction and shape 
may be as shown in Fig. 1 to 4.

6. Push Handle/ End Racks, Stakes and Superstructure — Push handles, end racks, stakes and 
superstructure may be fixed or removable and left to the discretion of the manufacturer or agreement 
between the manufacturer and the purchaser to meet problems of holding load on truck. 



rS: 8049 -1988

8. Tolerances — Tolerances on platform size and overall height shall be ±5 mm. 

9. Workmanship and Finish 

9.1 The platform truck shall be free from warp in structural frame work, blow holes and other defects 
, in casting. 

9.2 The painting shall conform to IS : 5-1978 'Colours for ready mixed paints and enamals ( third 
revision)'. 

9.3 The painted surface shall be free from wrinkles, irregular painting, dripping, scratches and 
irregularities in colouring. 

10. Performance 

10.1 When the platform truck is traversed over a smooth road loaded with 120 parcent of permissible 
carrying load, the truck wheels shall turn smoothly and swivel castor arrangem ants shall function 
satisfactorily. 

10.2 The platform truck shall be tested by applying the distributed load as given in Table 2 by leaving 
it for 10 minutes in this position. After completion of test there shall ba no permanent set or 
distortion in the structure or any member of the structure of the truck. 



TABLE 2 TEST LOADS 

( Clause 10.2) 


Carrying Load Capacity 

(kN) 


Distributed Load for Testing 

(kN) 


Up to 5 


Carrying load x 2 


OverS 


Carrying load x 1*5 



10.3 End racks and push handles shall withstand a minimum horizontal force equal to 230 N plus 
2 percent of rated capacity, without breaking or permanent bending. 

11. Wheels or Castors — The wheels/castors or combination thereof to be used for platform trucks 
shall conform to provisions of IS : 7369-1 983 'Specification for wheels and castors ( first revision )'. 



IS: 8049 -1988 

12. Designation — The platform truck shall be designated by its type, load carrying capacity and 
the number of this standard. 

Example 

A rcn-tilt type pletform truck with load carrying capacity of 10 kN shall be designated as: 

NT 10 IS: 8049 

13. Marking 

13.1 The platform truck shall be marked with the following information in visible position: 

a) Designation; 

b) Manufacturing number; 

c) Date of manufacture; and 

d) Ncme of the manufacturer or trade-mark, if any. 

13.2 Standard Marking— Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was published in 1976 on the basis of Japanese standard JIS B 8901-1957. It 
was first revised in 1983 taking into consideration the development on the subject at that time and 
to ir.ake it performance oriented. 

The second revision includes changes in tolerance on platform size and overall height. Some 
corrections have also been made in this revision. However, the interchangeably aspect of replace- 
able items, such as wheels and castors have been retained. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
